description:
Check the email sending setup status for a domain, including DNS record configuration progress.

ACCESS: needs a Proof account, signed in: call start_login, show the user its challenge, then wait_for_login, then call this tool again. Authenticating this client alone does NOT open this tool.
name: check_domain_email_status

actual_dns_host.description: The host serving the zone, when it differs from the provider that verified it.

api_verification.description: Set when the domain was added from an API verification, else null. Absent from an API that predates the field.

detected_provider.description: The DNS provider read from the nameservers; `unknown` when none matched.

email_sending_enabled.description: Never sent; read `for_email_sending`. Kept for released SDK types; removed in the next major.

email_verification.description: An email verification of the domain. The code itself is never returned.

godaddy_connected.description: Whether a GoDaddy connection is stored for this domain.

has_provider_credentials.description: Sent only by the add: the account already holds credentials for the detected provider.

oauth_connected.description: Whether a Cloudflare connection is stored for this domain.

oauth_url.description: Sent only by the add when Cloudflare sign-in is configured for the detected provider.

proof_expires_at.description: When that proof expires — the signed token's own `exp`. `proof_status` stays `active` after this instant (nothing rewrites it), so a client must compare against the clock to tell a live proof from an expired one. Proofs inside 30 days of expiry are renewed automatically while control can still be confirmed. Carried even when `proof_id` is null (a proof that predates the registry still has a signed expiry); null when the domain has no proof, or its proof never stored one.

proof_id.description: Public handle of the control proof backing this domain (`ph_ctl_<32 hex>`), resolved through the domain's mirroring asset — the same source `GET /me/assets` reads, so the two surfaces cannot disagree. Null when the domain has no proof, or when its proof predates the registry.

proof_revoked_reason.description: Reason the registry recorded, present only while `proof_status` is `revoked`.

proof_status.description: Registry status of that proof. A domain row can read `verified` while its proof is `revoked` — the row records that control was once shown, the proof records whether it still stands — so a client showing domain control must render THIS. Null means no registry record, which is NOT a revocation.

provider.description: Never sent; read `detected_provider`. Kept for released SDK types; removed in the next major.

provider_credential_name.description: Sent only by the add, with `has_provider_credentials`.

resend.description: Email-sending setup for a domain. Present once email sending has been set up.

status.description: Domain verification status. `verifying` while a check runs; `revoking` while the owner's removal or revocation cascade holds the domain; `reverification_required` after a revoked proof, until control is shown again.

supports_auto_dns.description: Whether the detected provider can create the verification record itself.

verification_subtype.description: How a provider verified the domain: by creating the record, or by confirming ownership without one.

verified_providers.description: Every provider (or `email`) that has confirmed control.
